skills.description: Create, adapt, evaluate, version, and retire Storyworld agent skills and workflows using pinned sources, trigger tests, context budgets, security review, provenance, and evidence-backed adoption proposals.
skills.purpose: Provide one governed lifecycle for Storyworld capabilities instead of ad hoc skill creation or bulk imports.
triggers: Create or materially revise a Storyworld skill, workflow, router, reference, or capability provenance record.
Evaluate trigger precision, context cost, output quality, security, portability, or upstream upgrade impact.
Deprecate, supersede, remove, or replace a capability.
inputs: existing Storyworld skill registry and routing graph
authoritative_sources: current task and applicable Storyworld instructions
pinned external sources as nonauthoritative evidence
preconditions: No source is imported until its exact revision and license are recorded.
Executable files, hooks, and installers remain disabled until separate security review.
A new skill is justified only when profiles or references cannot cover the capability.
workflow: Classify create, adapt, merge, evaluate, upgrade, deprecate, or retire.
Inspect existing skills and eliminate duplication.
Build a source and license ledger.
Choose the smallest execution shape and context budget.
Author or amend with minimal frontmatter and routed references.
Create should-trigger, should-not-trigger, working, holdout, and adversarial fixtures.
Run structural, security, routing, portability, and output-quality evaluations.
Produce an adoption or rejection proposal with replacement and rollback strategy.
prohibited: granting permission or adopting its own output
copying unclear or incompatible licensed content
creating duplicate skills when a reference/profile suffices
removing authority or evidence rules merely to reduce tokens
skills.failure: Stop and mark blocked when license, source, authority, trigger precision, or executable safety is unresolved. Preserve the prior capability unchanged.
skills.relationship: Owns the lifecycle of Storyworld capability packages; invokes security-review, fixture-authoring, decision-impact-analysis, and conformance-and-release as needed.

skills.description: Diagnose Storyworld bugs, failed checks, unknown outcomes, provider errors, workflow failures, and cross-component regressions through reproducible root-cause investigation before implementing a bounded fix.
skills.purpose: Prevent guess-and-patch debugging across Storyworld’s authority, workflow, provider, media, and storage boundaries.
triggers: A bug, failed check, performance regression, unknown outcome, provider callback inconsistency, data leak, or unexpected state is reported.
Two attempted fixes have not resolved the same symptom.
authoritative_sources: task-scoped logs/traces that satisfy redaction policy
preconditions: No fix is proposed before reproduction or a documented evidence-collection plan.
Diagnostics must not expose credentials, restricted payloads, or unrelated tenants.
Unknown outcomes remain unknown until reconciled.
workflow: Read the complete error and reproduce consistently.
Map the data, authority, and workflow boundaries crossed.
Compare with the nearest working path.
Trace the first divergence and state one falsifiable root-cause hypothesis.
Test one variable with the smallest safe experiment.
Create a failing regression fixture.
Implement one bounded root-cause fix.
Run fresh scoped and regression verification.
After repeated failed hypotheses, stop and request architectural review rather than stacking fixes.
prohibited: making multiple unrelated changes in one hypothesis test
changing accepted architecture to make a test pass
claiming a provider job failed or succeeded without reconciliation
validation: original symptom reproduced or evidence limitation recorded
regression fixture fails before and passes after
no new cross-tenant or authority regression
skills.failure: Return blocked with the missing evidence and safest next diagnostic action. Escalate for architectural review after repeated nonconfirming hypotheses or evidence of systemic coupling.
skills.relationship: Runs under governed-change; uses fixture-authoring and conformance-and-release; does not replace security-review for security incidents.

skills.description: Design, implement, review, and migrate Storyworld PostgreSQL and object-storage behavior with tenant isolation, RLS, transactions, exact versions, query evidence, backup and restore, reconciliation, and portable replacement boundaries.
skills.purpose: Provide a dedicated database/storage discipline for Storyworld’s modular monolith and content-addressed custody model.
triggers: Change tables, columns, indexes, migrations, RLS, transactions, SQL, search, database functions, storage records, blob reconciliation, backup, restore, or query performance.
Investigate cross-tenant visibility, locks, bloat, connection exhaustion, or slow queries.
authoritative_sources: accepted Storyworld contracts and module ownership
preconditions: Every change names the owning module and invariant.
Production DDL or data access requires explicit task authority.
RLS is never disabled to simplify tests.
Blob identity and semantic asset authority remain separate.
workflow: Map domain ownership, tenant scope, and transaction boundary.
Design additive migration and rollback/recovery path.
Define RLS and cross-tenant negative cases.
Inspect query plans and indexes with representative data.
Implement through repository migration conventions.
Test transactions, conflicts, retries, and idempotency.
Verify backup, restore, or reconciliation when custody is affected.
Record operational and replacement implications.
prohibited: treating object-store paths as semantic identity
claiming performance improvement without representative measurement
validation: migration up/down or recovery test as applicable
skills.failure: Fail closed on uncertain tenant isolation, migration reversibility, data-loss risk, or custody reconciliation. Require owner/DB review before proceeding.
skills.relationship: Composes with contract-authoring, schema-evolution, asset-custody-and-lineage, security-review, and conformance-and-release.
